newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank task force wants leeway on mergers.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank task force wants leeway on mergers.

text.p: A task force on the future of Canada's financial services industry told the government on Friday it should put an end to its policy of banning large financial institutions from merging or acquiring one another.

The task force did not make any recommendations on the subject of mergers between the six biggest Canadian banks, which dominate the industry, but looked instead at expansion by the major banks through the acquisition of other financial institutions.

Transactions between any large financial institutions, except the six biggest Canadian banks, should "be reviewed for approval on their merits," the task force said in preliminary recommendations to the government.
The task force was asked to make recommendations after moves by the big banks to expand through the acquisition of a trust company and a large insurance company.
"A 'big shall not buy big' policy, as it affects transactions between entities other than two .... (major) banks, should not have general application," the task force said.
It also recommended that government regulators take a close look at the impact of mergers on local and regional competition.
Jim Peterson, the secretary of state for international financial institutions, asked the task force last month to advise him on mergers and acquisitions in the Canadian financial services sector.
He made the request after Bank of Nova Scotia made a C$1.25 billion takeover offer for National Trustco Inc and Royal Bank of Canada launched a C$2.4 billion bid for London Insurance Group Inc.

While Peterson did not ask for recommendations specific to the two offers, he rquested that the task force suggest guidelines on how to handle major takeovers in the financial services industry. He said the request had been prompted by the two proposed takeovers.
Any acquisition of a financial institution in Canada requires the approval of the finance minister, on the recommendation of the superintendent of financial institutions.
The task force's full report is due in September 1998.

The preliminary report also recommended that the director of the federal competition bureau share information on a confidential basis with the fnance dpartment and the office of the superintendent of financial institutions when assessing mergers in the industry.
It said regulatory bodies should set guidelines to ensure ustomers are informed of implications of mergers.
"I will be reviewing the task force recommendations carefully," Peterson said in a statement. "Their views will provide valuable input to the process of assessing proposed transactions."
